speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment of your 8-month-old's feeding difficulties and abdominal distension, have these symptoms been present since birth, or did they develop more recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby ever successfully passed meconium within the first 24 hours of life, and do you notice any bilious (green) vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's Disease. The history of delayed meconium passage (implied by the current distension and failure to pass stool) combined with bilious vomiting and abdominal distension in an infant is highly suggestive of this condition. I recommend an immediate Abdominal_X-Ray to confirm fecal loading and rule out obstruction, followed by a contrast enema.
